pill.desc: white to light pink, free-flowing suspension in a single-dose vial

tell: A half-life of 5.6 to 11.5 weeks, driven by slow release from the injection site, sets this long-acting integrase inhibitor apart.

clues.text: Absorbed slowly from the injection site, and over 99.8% is bound to plasma protein. Feces carry 59% of the dose, 47% of it unchanged.
The active moiety has a molecular weight of 405.35 g/mol, and it is formulated as a free-flowing extended-release suspension with mannitol and polyethylene glycol.
Approved under an NDA as single-dose vials of 600 mg per 3 mL, given every two months after two monthly starting injections.
Boxed warning: drug-resistant variants arise in people with undiagnosed infection, so testing precedes each injection. Contraindicated with rifampin or rifapentine.
Pre-exposure prophylaxis to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 infection in adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg.
An HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor.
The generic name begins with C and has twelve letters.
